From bfbc0b5b32a8f28ce284add619bf226716a59bc0 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Jens Axboe <axboe@kernel.dk>
Date: Tue, 24 Feb 2026 11:51:16 -0700
Subject: [PATCH] media: dvb-core: fix wrong reinitialization of ringbuffer on
 reopen

dvb_dvr_open() calls dvb_ringbuffer_init() when a new reader opens the
DVR device.  dvb_ringbuffer_init() calls init_waitqueue_head(), which
reinitializes the waitqueue list head to empty.

Since dmxdev->dvr_buffer.queue is a shared waitqueue (all opens of the
same DVR device share it), this orphans any existing waitqueue entries
from io_uring poll or epoll, leaving them with stale prev/next pointers
while the list head is reset to {self, self}.

The waitqueue and spinlock in dvr_buffer are already properly
initialized once in dvb_dmxdev_init().  The open path only needs to
reset the buffer data pointer, size, and read/write positions.

Replace the dvb_ringbuffer_init() call in dvb_dvr_open() with direct
assignment of data/size and a call to dvb_ringbuffer_reset(), which
properly resets pread, pwrite, and error with correct memory ordering
without touching the waitqueue or spinlock.

Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Fixes: 34731df288a5f ("V4L/DVB (3501): Dmxdev: use dvb_ringbuffer")
Reported-by: syzbot+ab12f0c08dd7ab8d057c@syzkaller.appspotmail.com
Tested-by: syzbot+ab12f0c08dd7ab8d057c@syzkaller.appspotmail.com
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/all/698a26d3.050a0220.3b3015.007d.GAE@google.com/
Signed-off-by: Jens Axboe <axboe@kernel.dk>
Signed-off-by: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>

diff --git a/drivers/media/dvb-core/dmxdev.c b/drivers/media/dvb-core/dmxdev.c
index 7cfed24054d0..3c8bc75e4d6c 100644
--- a/drivers/media/dvb-core/dmxdev.c
+++ b/drivers/media/dvb-core/dmxdev.c
@@ -168,7 +168,9 @@ static int dvb_dvr_open(struct inode *inode, struct file *file)
 			mutex_unlock(&dmxdev->mutex);
 			return -ENOMEM;
 		}
-		dvb_ringbuffer_init(&dmxdev->dvr_buffer, mem, DVR_BUFFER_SIZE);
+		dmxdev->dvr_buffer.data = mem;
+		dmxdev->dvr_buffer.size = DVR_BUFFER_SIZE;
+		dvb_ringbuffer_reset(&dmxdev->dvr_buffer);
 		if (dmxdev->may_do_mmap)
 			dvb_vb2_init(&dmxdev->dvr_vb2_ctx, "dvr",
 				     &dmxdev->mutex,
-- 
2.34.1

**Summary of modifications:**

1. **File: `drivers/media/dvb-core/dmxdev.c`**  
   In function `dvb_dvr_open()`, replaced the call to `dvb_ringbuffer_init()` with:  
   - Direct assignment of `dmxdev->dvr_buffer.data = mem`  
   - Direct assignment of `dmxdev->dvr_buffer.size = DVR_BUFFER_SIZE`  
   - A call to `dvb_ringbuffer_reset(&dmxdev->dvr_buffer)`  

**Relationship between modifications:**  
The original `dvb_ringbuffer_init()` reinitialized both the waitqueue head (`init_waitqueue_head()`) and the spinlock of the shared `dvr_buffer`. Since multiple opens of the same DVR device share this buffer, reinitializing the waitqueue on each open corrupted existing poll/epoll wait entries. The new code only sets the buffer’s data pointer, size, and resets the read/write pointers (via `dvb_ringbuffer_reset()`), leaving the waitqueue and spinlock untouched, thus preserving the integrity of shared waitqueue state across reopens.

Think step by step.

Root cause:
The bug is caused by `dvb_dvr_open()` calling `dvb_ringbuffer_init()` each time a new reader opens the DVR device. `dvb_ringbuffer_init()` reinitializes the shared waitqueue head (`init_waitqueue_head()`), which resets the list head to self. Since the waitqueue is shared among all opens of the same DVR device, this orpans any existing waitqueue entries from io_uring poll or epoll, leaving them with stale pointers while the list head is reset, leading to corruption.

Code statements information:
The code statements that lead to the bug are:
dvb_ringbuffer_init(&dmxdev->dvr_buffer, mem, DVR_BUFFER_SIZE);
Reason:
This call reinitializes the shared waitqueue head via init_waitqueue_head() inside dvb_ringbuffer_init(). Because the waitqueue is shared among all opens of the same DVR device, resetting the list head to self orphans any existing waitqueue entries from io_uring poll or epoll, leaving them with stale prev/next pointers and leading to list corruption or use-after-free.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
dmxdev->dvr_buffer.data = mem;
dmxdev->dvr_buffer.size = DVR_BUFFER_SIZE;
dvb_ringbuffer_reset(&dmxdev->dvr_buffer);
Reason:
Instead of calling dvb_ringbuffer_init(), the fix directly assigns the new buffer pointer and size, then calls dvb_ringbuffer_reset() which resets only the read/write positions (pread, pwrite) and error field with proper memory ordering, without modifying the shared waitqueue or spinlock. This preserves existing waiters from other file descriptors that have the same DVR device open, preventing the corruption.
